iut_type: Compliance Folder (CD-R) shipment logistics -- Japan Post Click Post mail service restriction on enclosed correspondence documents (shinsho)
customer_question: We received the Compliance Folder (disk), but the delivery slip wasn't included in the package -- could we get that too?
question_variants: Why wasn't a delivery slip included with the physically shipped Compliance Folder?
Can invoices or delivery slips be physically enclosed with a Click Post package?
actual_issue: The customer received the physically shipped Compliance Folder CD-R but found no delivery slip enclosed in the package, and asked for one to be provided.
plain_english_explanation: Japan Post's Click Post service (a low-cost tracked small-parcel mail service, used here to ship the Compliance Folder CD-R) cannot legally be used to send 'shinsho' -- a category of correspondence documents defined under Japanese postal regulations that includes items like invoices and delivery slips. Because of this restriction, the delivery slip could not be physically enclosed with the CD-R shipment and instead had to be sent separately as an email attachment.
consultant_answer: Click Post mail service doesn't allow enclosing correspondence documents (shinsho), so our sales contact sent the delivery slip separately by email earlier today -- I've attached it to this email as well for your confirmation.
decision_logic: When shipping a Compliance Folder or similar physical deliverable via Japan Post's Click Post service, any accompanying invoice, delivery slip, or other document classified as shinsho under Japanese postal regulations cannot be physically enclosed in the same package and must be sent separately (e.g., by email).
final_recommendation: When shipping deliverables via a low-cost tracked mail service like Click Post, proactively send accompanying invoices/delivery slips via a separate channel (email) at the same time, rather than waiting for the customer to notice the document is missing from the physical package and ask for it.
risk_if_done_wrong: A customer expecting the delivery slip to be physically enclosed with the shipped package may delay their internal accounts-payable process (which depends on receiving that document) if they don't realize it was sent separately by email.
